questions.question: In this model, which side is the cleft on?
Where is the gap that the operation fills?
questions.expected: In the bone that holds the teeth (gum bone), next to the front teeth, under the gum

questions.question: Which tooth is missing in this model, and how common is that in children with a cleft?
questions.expected: The small tooth next to the front tooth (lateral incisor); about half of children with a cleft

questions.question: Why does the adult eye tooth need the bone graft?
questions.expected: It needs bone to come down / grow into

questions.question: At about what age is the bone graft usually done?
Where does the bone for the graft most often come from?
What has changed about 3 months after the operation?
questions.expected: New bone fills the gap (joins the two parts of the jaw) and the gum has healed over it

questions.question: How and when do doctors check that the new bone has taken?
questions.expected: An X-ray at about 3 to 6 months

questions.question: What might you feel where the bone was taken?
questions.expected: The hip can be sore for a while

questions.question: Years later, where is the eye tooth?
questions.expected: It came down through the new bone into the row of teeth

questions.question: What lines up the teeth in the later stage?
What are the choices for the gap left by the tooth that never grew?
questions.expected: Move the eye tooth into the gap and reshape it; or keep the gap (false tooth on a removable plate while growing, then an implant or a bridge)
